mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the following 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 4.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during two consecutive quarters of declining GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) below 2.5% over the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which reduces uncertainty and supports risk assets, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL < 2.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in months where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL < 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average combined with a rise in personal savings (RSAFS) signals improved household balance sheets and housing demand, which boosts consumer spending expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average AND RSAFS > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of PAYEMS > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) growth and S&P 500 returns exists at the 60-day horizon; when quarterly GDPC1 growth exceeds 2%, the S&P 500 tends to deliver positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When quarterly GDPC1 growth exceeds 2%, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10).
